**Wednesday, 11 November 2026 · 14:30–16:00 · Helmholtzweg 4, SR 6 Physik**

We will start with the first marimo notebook, have a short lecture on training and testing, then spend most of the remaining time working with the ML MolSim material. We will see how far we get; finishing the whole practical is not the goal for this shorter session.

## Bring and prepare

Bring a laptop and charger. Follow the [setup guide](../setup.qmd) as far as you can; bring any error message rather than spending hours on installation. Download the [introductory kit](../downloads/introductory-setup.zip) and the [MOF practical kit](../downloads/mof-practical.zip), and extract them into separate folders.

## 1. Basic Python in marimo · about 20 minutes

Open **`00-getting-started.py`**, our first notebook. From the extracted introductory-kit folder:

```bash
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked marimo edit notebooks/00-getting-started.py --headless
```

Open the local URL printed in the terminal. Work through variables, arithmetic, lists, and a small function. Change a concentration, follow which cells update, and check a prediction by hand. Investigate the deliberately flawed error calculation, then save and reopen your own copy. Ask a partner to explain one line back to you.

[Notebook source](../notebooks/00-getting-started.py) · [Recorded preview](../notebooks/previews/00-getting-started.html)

## 2. Short lecture: training and testing · about 10–15 minutes

We will connect the calculation to the basic modelling workflow:

- **Inputs, target, and parameters:** what the model receives, predicts, and fits.
- **Training and a loss:** use observations to fit parameters; a small training error alone does not establish useful predictions.
- **Validation and testing:** use validation data to compare choices, then assess the chosen procedure on reserved test data. Decide what a new chemical case should mean before interpreting a score.

The [learning-from-data notes](../lectures/02-learning-from-data.qmd) provide the fuller explanation. We will use the remaining time to put these ideas into practice.

## 3. Hands-on ML MolSim · the remaining time

From the separately extracted MOF-kit folder:

```bash
uv sync --locked --group mof
uv run --locked --group mof marimo edit notebooks/03-mof-uptake.py --headless
```

This is our adaptation of the ML MolSim gas-uptake practical. It predicts **simulated CO₂ uptake** from geometric descriptions of porous materials. Start with the data and work at your own pace, alone or with a partner:

1. Identify a row, the input features, and the target with its units and conditions.
2. Inspect the training, validation, and test split. Establish a simple baseline.
3. Fit and compare models using validation results. Record one change and what it did.
4. **If we reach this step:** write down the model choice before revealing the final test results. Explain what that test can and cannot establish.

Keep the test checkbox unchecked while choosing a model. We can continue unfinished comparisons in the next class.

[MOF practical notes](../lectures/03-mof-uptake.qmd) · [Notebook source](../notebooks/03-mof-uptake.py) · [Recorded preview](../notebooks/previews/03-mof-uptake.html)

## Alongside the practical: collect project ideas

Keep the **shared project-ideas document from the course email** open. Whenever a question occurs to you, add a few lines: the chemical question, possible data, a first comparison, and what help you need. Rough ideas are welcome; this is not an assessed proposal. Comment on related ideas if you would like to collaborate.

Before leaving, save your notebook, record where you stopped, and leave one project idea or question. We will use these notes to plan the next steps together.
